category_labels_final.attribution_authorship_disclosure_integr: Attribution, authorship, disclosure and ethics integrity

category_explanations_final.research_content_reliability: Signals that the reliability, reproducibility, validity, or evidentiary integrity of the research content itself is questioned. Includes data, image, methods/materials, analyses, results/conclusions, non-reproducibility, paper-mill and AI/computer-generated content signals when the official definition concerns article-content reliability.
category_explanations_final.attribution_authorship_disclosure_integr: Signals concerning authorship, affiliation, consent/approval to publish, plagiarism, duplicate publication, citation/reference/attribution, copyright/ownership, conflicts of interest, or research-ethics disclosure/approval. This is an integrity/relationship-transparency family, not a blame category.
category_explanations_final.editorial_peer_review_governance: Signals concerning peer-review integrity, editorial decision-making, rogue/editorial breach, journal/publisher error, or governance of the pre-publication editorial process. Investigation-by-journal/publisher alone is not treated as editorial fault.
category_explanations_final.post_publication_transparency_due_proces: Signals concerning investigation source, official/institutional/third-party oversight, notice transparency, communication, objection, correction/retraction status, removal/availability, or legal/ORI/misconduct process. This category means post-publication process/oversight metadata, not due-process failure or fault by the named actor.

main_figure_rule: Use maincat_* flags generated only from reason items with main_figure_recommended=true. cat_* flags preserve broader semantic/audit category assignments.
guardrails: Retraction Watch Reason terms remain non-exclusive curated metadata, not fault or liability determinations.
Post-publication process/oversight signals include investigation-source and procedural-communication reasons, but do not imply that the investigating actor caused the problem.
Broad misconduct labels should not be expanded into research-content, attribution, or editorial-governance categories unless the official definition specifies the mechanism.
Status-only notice/update/removal reasons can retain an audit category but should have main_figure_recommended=false unless they are used in a separate transparency/metadata figure.
